_comment: Registration for scripts/check-ci-coverage.py (issue #1146).
WHY THIS GATE NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): it is a gate that lets work
THROUGH. `make verify` reads its green and nothing downstream re-derives
whether a gate is dispositioned against CI. It is also read by a DIFFERENT
session than the one that wrote the declaration - the author declares, the
reviewer and the pipeline consume - and a reader cannot see what produced
the green.
AND THE GREEN IS ESPECIALLY CHEAP TO FAKE HERE. The subject of this gate is
an ACCOUNTING, and a short honest accounting and a short blind one print the
same confident line. #1146's own defect was exactly that: `make verify` ran
27 gates, CI ran 16, and nothing in the tree could say so - not because
anything reported wrongly, but because nothing reported at all. A gate that
counted declarations instead of checking them would reproduce that silence
while looking like its remedy, which is what the anchor is.
THE CASES ARE WHOLE FIXTURE TREES - a three-target Makefile and a two-step
pipeline - because this gate's subject is the RELATIONSHIP between two files,
and neither file alone can express a case. Each bad tree breaks ONE of the
distinctions the gate draws; a control exercising one leaves the rest
unproven:
bad-undeclared-gate          the ordinary shape: a gate is added to
`verify:` and nobody says what CI does with
it. This is #1146 itself, in one tree.
bad-declared-runs-no-step    a declaration that CLAIMS a step the pipeline
has not got. The Makefile side is complete and
well-formed, so a gate reading only the
declarations scores this clean - and the tree
is WORSE than the undeclared one, because a
reader who checked the annotation comes away
more confident and equally wrong. Deleting a
step is the ordinary way this arises.
bad-malformed-verb           `ci: run alpha-check`, one letter short. The
reason vocabulary is open on purpose, and a
parser lenient enough to honour that turns
'an unrecognised reason still passes' into 'a
malformed declaration still passes'.
bad-excluded-with-no-reason  `ci: excluded` with nothing after it. ITS OWN
CASE, not folded into the verb typo: they fail
different halves of the grammar - an
unrecognised KEYWORD and a missing ARGUMENT -
and a parser matching on the first word alone
catches the typo and passes this. One tree
carrying both would still red on the typo,
leaving the half it was added for unproven.
bad-declaration-bound-to-a-ghost-target
a complete, well-formed `ci: excluded
needs-git` sitting DIRECTLY ABOVE the
undeclared gate, naming `beta-chek`. The
correct gate answers this identically to
bad-undeclared-gate, which is the point: the
two trees discriminate between binding by NAME
and binding by POSITION, and a positional
reader passes this one. `verify-coverage-check`
chose name-binding and documented why; this
case is what holds the inherited decision.
THE GOOD CASE IS NOT JUST THE PASSING PATH. It carries both dispositions at
once - a `runs` whose step exists and an `excluded` with a reason - and its
`verify:` rule is written ACROSS A LINE CONTINUATION, which is the exact
reformat that would empty the first population. A gate wedged at 'fail' is
indistinguishable from a working one on the bad cases alone, and this gate is
a `make verify` prerequisite, so a false red blocks every merge in the
repository.
THE TWO EMPTY-POPULATION CASES ARE NOT HERE, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE
REGISTER RATHER THAN A GAP. A tree with no `verify:` target and a tree whose
pipeline is written in YAML's list form both make this gate exit 2 UNKNOWN,
and both are committed - at tests/fixtures/ci-coverage/, driven by
tests/test_ci_coverage_check.py, which asserts the exit code and the named
population. They cannot be registered HERE because `expect: UNKNOWN` routes a
case to the anchor-SANITY loop, where the anchor must AGREE (the cost is
stated in check-negative-controls.py beside `sanity_cases`, and measured for
the one control that registers an UNKNOWN case today). For THIS gate the two
requirements are mutually exclusive by construction: the anchor's blindness
under test is that it never derives the prerequisite population, and an
anchor that refused an empty one would have to derive it - at which point it
catches bad-undeclared-gate and is no longer blind. So the guard is held by
the suite, whose red `make test` and CI `validate` both consume.
Stdlib-only, git-free and offline, like the gate: the fixtures need no binary
the slim CI image lacks, so the control gives the same verdict there as here.

cases.name: bad-undeclared-gate
cases.why: A `verify` prerequisite with no `ci:` clause. If this scores GOOD the gate cannot see an undispositioned gate at all, which is the whole of #1146 in one tree.

cases.name: bad-declared-runs-no-step
cases.why: `ci: runs ghost-step` against a pipeline with no such step. Every declaration here is present and well-formed, so a gate that read only the Makefile scores this tree clean - and this tree is the worse failure, because the annotation makes a reader MORE confident.

cases.name: bad-malformed-verb
cases.why: `ci: run alpha-check` - the verb one letter short. The reason vocabulary is deliberately open, and a parser lenient enough to honour that will accept this unless the SHAPE is strict; then the gate is green over a gate nobody dispositioned.

cases.name: bad-excluded-with-no-reason
cases.why: `ci: excluded` with no reason. An empty reason is a missing ARGUMENT, not an open-vocabulary one. Separate from the verb typo because a first-word parser catches that and passes this.

cases.name: bad-declaration-bound-to-a-ghost-target
cases.why: A well-formed declaration naming `beta-chek`, sitting directly above the real `beta-check`. Proves the clause is read by NAME and not by POSITION: a positional reader binds it to the target below and scores the tree clean.

cases.name: good-fully-declared
cases.why: Both dispositions at once - a `runs` whose step exists, an `excluded` with a reason - over a `verify:` rule written across a line continuation, which is the reformat that would empty the first population. THE HALF THAT MATTERS for a gate wedged at 'fail': this gate is a `make verify` prerequisite, so a false red blocks every merge in the repository.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the gate is new, so there is no previous blind version to vendor. What IS on the record is the framing that preceded it - commit a9408bc of this same issue appended a `ci:` clause to all 27 gates and reported '22 runs, 5 excluded', a number obtained by grepping the Makefile. This file is that grep. It counts declarations and checks neither side, so it MISSES all five known-bad inputs and AGREES with the real gate on the known-good one.
